slot.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slot.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges
slot.brief: Compare de Broglie wavelengths of an electron accelerated through given p.d. vs a proton/alpha with same KE; multi-step ratio with sqrt(m) scaling.

stem: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of $600$ V, while an $\alpha$ particle is accelerated from rest through $300$ V. Given that the $\alpha$ particle has charge $+2e$ and mass $4m_p$, what is the ratio $\lambda_e/\lambda_\alpha$?

verdicts.working: Using \(\lambda=h/\sqrt{2mqV}\), both particles gain kinetic energy \(600e\). Thus \(\lambda_e/\lambda_\alpha=\sqrt{4m_p/m_e}=2\sqrt{m_p/m_e}\).

working:
$K_e=e(600\ \text{V})=600e\ \text{V}$; $K_\alpha=2e(300\ \text{V})=600e\ \text{V}$
$\lambda=h/\sqrt{2mK}$
$\dfrac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_\alpha}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_\alpha K_\alpha}{m_e K_e}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{4m_p}{m_e}}=2\sqrt{\dfrac{m_p}{m_e}}$

Independent check: Using \(\lambda=h/\sqrt{2mqV}\), both particles gain kinetic energy \(600e\). Thus \(\lambda_e/\lambda_\alpha=\sqrt{4m_p/m_e}=2\sqrt{m_p/m_e}\).
